text:
mike: Quick question — SOC customer wants a downloadable 'who changed what' export that includes routing policy id, actor id, and the canary rollout tag. They also want attachable justification text. How do we avoid leaking PII/credentials in exports?

sophia: We currently include actor.display_name + actor.email in the console, but exports are ndjson with full actor object. That seems risky for eDiscovery.

jordan: Can we add an export mode: minimal / contextual / full? minimal = actor id + role; contextual = display_name + UI breadcrumbs; full = raw actor with email. Gate full by admin entitlement.

anna_product: +1 for modes. Also product asks for a small UI badge indicating what mode was used to generate the export. Compliance teams need provenance.

kate_legal: Legal wants two safety features: automatic redaction of email addresses unless tenant-admin consented, and an auditable consent timestamp stored with the export. Also we need TTL for downloadable links.

mike: Implementation-wise: do we add entitlement check at the export API (backend) or generate a signed bundle from the export service after applying redaction? Which keeps responsibility clearer for Dedicated/Private customers?

jordan: Backend entitlement check first. Then hand off to export worker to assemble NDJSON bundles. That worker should apply configured redaction rules per-tenant. This lets Private deployments override redaction config.

infra-bot: deploy: export-worker v2.3 queued to prod.

mike: What about showing 'who changed' details inline in Console vs in export? We might keep inline richer but exports stricter by default.

sophia: I worry about divergence — devs will assume console == export. Need explicit console copy indicator and a small warning CTA when exporting: "This file may contain contact info — verify export mode."

anna_product: Also think about routing policy ids: customers want human-friendly names in exports so they can map to change requests. But names can change over time; we should include both id and current display_name.

jordan: Good point. Export entry shape suggestion: { event_ts, resource_type, resource_id, resource_name, change_summary, actor_id, actor_display_name (optional), actor_email (redacted unless allowed), justification, rollout_tag, export_mode } — we should keep schema backwards compatible.

kate_legal: Include export_mode and consent_ts. For redaction, we need to record what was redacted (e.g., fields redacted) so downstream auditors know something was removed.

mike: How do we surface that in Console? A small 'export provenance' panel that lists: mode, who exported, when, redaction summary, and signed checksum of the bundle.

jordan: Technically easy: export metadata row in ledger with JSON metadata. But we must be careful storing PII in that ledger; metadata should itself obey redaction rules. Maybe store hashed email for owner-of-export, and keep human-readable only in the signed bundle.

sophia: Re quotas: big tenants could request huge exports. We should have quota + queueing + preflight estimate. Preflight returns estimated bytes + tokenized count and requires a consent action for full exports.

mike: Good. Add a rate limit: one full export per tenant per 24h unless higher-tier. Also preflight + charge-estimate (counts against export quota).

anna_product: UX note: UI should show preflight results with an inline "redaction preview" sample (like first 5 lines) so admins can confirm before download. Keep sample scrubbed in minimal mode.

jordan: For API shape, propose POST /v1/tenants/:id/exports with body { query, mode, include_rollout_tags, include_justifications } -> returns preflight_id or export_job_id. Then GET /v1/exports/:job tarball. We'll version as v2.

kate_legal: Need an explicit audit event when export is requested and when file is downloaded. Those events must be immutable and include the consented policy version id.

mike: Misc: Should we sign bundles (kid + signature) so downstream SIEMs can verify authenticity?

jordan: Yes — signed tar + manifest.json with checksum and signature. Manifest contains export metadata (mode, redaction summary, signer_kid).

sophia: Edgecase: if resource names contain sensitive tokens (someone pasted credentials in policy name). We should run a simple PII scanner during preflight and flag any high-risk fields for redaction, with explanation.

anna_product: Sounds like a lot — timeline? We need a minimal MVP: endpoint + modes + preflight + admin consent + signed bundle + UI badge + 24h quota. Post-MVP: redaction scanner, per-field redaction audit, per-tenant overrides.

mike: Proposed owners: jordan (backend export worker), sophia (console UI + sample preview), anna_product (product requirements), kate_legal (compliance signoff). I'll open a RFC and attach this thread. Any objections?

kate_legal: No objections. Will review RFC for legal language.

jordan: I'll draft API proto and sample NDJSON schema. Expect PR early next week.

infra-bot: ci/status: export-worker tests passed (18/18).

mike: Thanks — will tag in RFC and schedule a short sync to lock schema. :thumbsup:
